envelope.description: Wire the reconcile into maintenance.update after the build step

body.title: Wire the reconcile into maintenance.update after the build step
body.summary: Insert the reconcile between src/cli/services/maintenance.ts:112 and :114 — strictly after git fetch/merge and `npm run build`, never before — using the t7 wrapper and the t10 `loadBuiltCatalog` resolution (fall back to defer-to-boot and report the deferral when it returns null). It must run unconditionally (no opt-in flag) and write at most once, only when changed. Because every failure path in update() early-returns `ok: false` (L55/65/75/84/88/99/109) and the whole body sits in one try/catch returning ok:false (L116-118), the non-fatal requirement needs its OWN inner try/catch — a naive throw would flip a successful update to failed. On success populate configReconcile with counts and push 'reconcile' onto the existing `steps` channel; on failure capture the message into configReconcile.error while still returning ok:true, and report a ConfigCatalogError distinguishably (an explicit shipped-catalog-bug message, not an anonymous failure string) so it is not flattened into the same channel as a user-config or I/O failure. onLog carries the per-key detail the LLD requires, not just counts: emit exactly one reconcile summary line plus one detail line per filled and per repaired key naming its catalog dot-path, and for an ancestor collision the detail line also names the discarded scalar value so the loss is stated, not hidden. An explicit no-change line or an explicit failure line is emitted when there is nothing filled or repaired — never silence — and onLog is the only progress channel. Add the rationale comment for the stale-catalog resolution at this call site, and an acceptance-visible pointer to the t7 deviation note covering s8-sbdry3 (the CLI writing ~/.insrc/config.json directly). Ship the update integration tests (stubbed git/build steps, recording onLog collector) alongside.
acceptanceChecks: The reconcile call sits after the build push and before the final `return { ok: true, steps }`; an ordering assertion over the stubbed steps proves it never precedes git-pull or build

A reconcile failure after successful git-pull + build still returns ok:true with the reason in configReconcile.error and on onLog, and a ConfigCatalogError is reported with a distinguishable shipped-catalog-bug message
onLog emits exactly one reconcile summary line plus one detail line per filled and per repaired key, each naming the catalog dot-path; counts stay in configReconcile
A reconcile that repairs an ancestor collision emits a detail line containing both the colliding catalog path and the discarded scalar value
An explicit no-change onLog line is emitted when nothing was filled or repaired; a silent no-op fails the test
The reconcile is wrapped in its own inner try/catch, verified by a test where the reconcile throws and update still returns ok:true
git-pull and build behaviour is byte-identical to the pre-change baseline and no UpdateOptions flag was added
The stale-catalog resolution is exercised: loadBuiltCatalog's freshly built catalog is used, and a null return falls back to defer-to-boot and reports the deferral rather than a no-change result
The call site carries the stale-catalog rationale comment and references the t7 deviation note covering the CLI-writes-config-directly question (s8-sbdry3)

tests.name: maintenance.update — ordering assertion over the stubbed steps proves the reconcile is sequenced strictly after git-pull and build

maintenance.update — success populates MaintenanceResult.configReconcile {changed, filled, repaired} and emits exactly one onLog summary line plus one detail line per filled and per repaired key naming its catalog dot-path
maintenance.update — nothing filled or repaired emits an explicit no-change onLog line; silence fails the test
maintenance.update — an ancestor-collision repair emits a detail line naming both the colliding catalog path and the discarded scalar value

maintenance.update — reconcile failure after successful git-pull + build still returns ok:true with the reason in configReconcile.error and on onLog; a ConfigCatalogError is reported with a distinguishable shipped-catalog-bug message
maintenance.update — a throwing reconcile is caught by its own inner try/catch and update still returns ok:true
maintenance.update — no new UpdateOptions flag, reconcile runs unconditionally, git-pull + build behaviour byte-identical to the pre-change baseline

maintenance.update — stale-catalog resolution exercised: the post-build loadBuiltCatalog result is used, and a null return falls back to defer-to-boot reporting the deferral instead of a confident no-change against the in-memory pre-update catalog
